5. Mr. Abdus Samad, the Learned senior advocate for the appellant submitted that the law barred the application of the plaintiffs as it was made long after the award was made on 15.10.1996. Ile submitted that the Court fell in error in condoning the delay under Article 181 of the Limitation Act as said Article was not applicable in view of Article 178 clearly providing for a period of limitation in making such application. 

 7. Submission of Mr. Samad on limitation appears to be correct. Article 181 of the Limitation Act is the residuary provision which can only he invoked when no period of limitation provided elsewhere in the schedule to the limitation Act for making such an application. Article 178 has clearly provided a period of 90 days for making of an application for filing the award in court from the date of service of notice of making of the award. The Court might have swayed away by a decision of a Division Bench of our Division in the case of Bazla Rice Mills Vs. Bangladesh (1989) 41 DLR 504. It was decided therein that one can tile an application under Section 14(2) of the Arbitration Act for an order directing the arbitrator or umpire to file the award in Court within a period of three years under Article 181 of the Limitation Act when he did not receive any notice of making the award. 

 9. Mr. Samad referred few letters which have been printed in a supplementary paper book but not adduced into evidence and submitted that when the plaintiff demanded money on the basis of the award in June, 1996, it must he held that the plaintiff had at least knowledge of making of the award. The simple answer is the knowledge of making of the award, if any, is not sufficient to fix one with the notice of making of the award within the meaning of Article 178 of the limitation Act. Cf, Indian Rayon Corporation V. Raunaq and Co (P) Ltd, (1988) 4 SSC 31. 

 13. Further, we find on 19.08.1999 the defendant appeared in Court and on 20.03.2002 filed the objections. Article 158 of the Limitation Act prescribes a period of 30 days for setting aside an award or to get an award remitted for reconsideration from the date of service of notice of filing of the award. It is true, the Court did not issue any notice of the filing of the award by the umpire. When the appellant took time on number of occasions to file written statement against the award, he had the clear knowledge of the filing of the award. In the circumstances no further notice was required under section 14(2) of the Arbitration Act to issue. 

 15. We are enable to accept such submission. Receipt of the written objection by the Court cannot be termed as condonation of the delay in making the objections. The defendant never sought for condonation of the delay by making any proper application. Limitation under Article 158 of the Limitation Act goes to the root of the right to set aside or get the award remitted for reconsideration: In the circumstances, there is no scope from the conclusion that the objections filed was out of time by more than a year and such objections did not deserve any consideration, and was, therefore liable to he rejected outright upon such ground of limitation alone. It was however rejected on merit.
